issue.title: Add test for configuration recovery when all input probabilities are zero

repository.name: qiskit-addon-sqd-hpc
repository.description: qiskit-addon-sqd-hpc is a modern C++17/20/23/26 software library to enable large-scale sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) calculations on HPC systems.

issue.body:
Adds a subcase to the `recover_configurations` tests in which every input probability is zero, so the recovered probabilities sum to zero. It checks that `internal::_normalize` skips the division instead of producing NaNs. Before this, that `sum == 0.0` branch was only reached when the output was empty, never with actual zero elements.

Both inputs (`0b0000` and `0b1111`) correct to `0b1111`, so the test also asserts that they are merged into a single output entry.

The flip weights in this test are nonzero (0.01), so it covers only output normalization, not the flip-weight division by zero from Qiskit/qiskit-addon-sqd#274. That exact NaN cannot arise here, because this port passes raw flip weights to `NoReplacementSampler` without normalizing them. A related all-zero-flip-weight case that *is* reachable here is tracked in #64.

@garrison Closes #33

issue.title: NoReplacementSampler aborts when all flip weights are zero in configuration recovery

repository.name: qiskit-addon-sqd-hpc
repository.description: qiskit-addon-sqd-hpc is a modern C++17/20/23/26 software library to enable large-scale sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) calculations on HPC systems.

issue.body:
Split out from #33, which asked for two things: a test with zero input probabilities (addressed in #63) and confirmation that this codebase doesn't share the defect in Qiskit/qiskit-addon-sqd#274.  This issue is the second half.

The good news: the specific NaN in #274 can't occur here, because this port never normalizes the flip weights — it passes raw weights to `internal::NoReplacementSampler` instead of dividing by their sum.

The bad news: the all-zero-flip-weight *condition* is still reachable, and we mishandle it.

```cpp
const std::vector<std::bitset<4>> bitstrings{0b1111};
const std::vector<double> probs(1, 1.0);
std::array<std::vector<double>, 2> occs{
    std::vector<double>(2, 1.0), std::vector<double>(2, 1.0)
};
auto [m, p] = recover_configurations(bitstrings, probs, occs, {0, 0}, rng);
```

Here `density_s == 0`, so `_p_flip_1_to_0(0.0, 1.0) == 0.0` for every orbital: `probs_table[s][1]` is all zeros while `num_flip == 2`.  The behavior then depends on build flags:

- **Hardened libstdc++ (`_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`):** aborts in `std::discrete_distribution::_M_initialize` on `assert(__sum > 0)`.  I get a core dump with a plain `g++ -std=c++17` build on a toolchain where those assertions are enabled by default.
- **`-O2 -DNDEBUG`:** constructs, then throws `std::runtime_error("Cannot draw more samples than number of nonzero weights.")`.

The `remaining_nonzero_weights == 0` guard in `operator()` (`sample-without-replacement.hpp:99`) can't prevent the abort, because `dist` is constructed in the member-initializer list at line 60 — before the validation loop body runs.  An all-zero weight sum is a precondition violation for `std::discrete_distribution`.

Two things worth deciding:

1. **Validate before constructing `dist`.**  Moving the weight validation ahead of the distribution's construction would make the failure deterministic across build configurations.  `subsampling.hpp:82-88` already does this kind of pre-check via `get_remaining_nonzero_weights()`; `_bipartite_bitstring_correcting` has no equivalent.
2. **Decide what the right behavior is.**  These are arguably legitimate inputs — fully saturated occupancies with a target Hamming weight below the current count.  `std::runtime_error` is also an odd choice next to the `std::invalid_argument` used by `recover_configurations`'s own validation, and the message is misleading when the caller asked for a single sample.

Once we settle on the intended behavior, that's the test that actually discharges the original ask in #33.
